hook: SCP-2980 is a short, light piece: a red plug-in nightlight that, at 8:30 every evening, brings a horned demon into the room to read you a bedtime story. It is mostly a joke told in Foundation format, so go in expecting a cheerful monster with reading glasses rather than horror. The stories themselves are where the dark humor sits.
whyItMatters:
The comedy runs on a demon who talks exactly like a self-help speaker or an author on a book tour. He is tired of the torture business, wants to give back, has a collection coming out next spring and a charity with an unpronounceable name.

It is also a neat example of how much a file can do with a list. The sample story summaries are each one line of children's-book setup followed by a hellish detail, and that rhythm does most of the work.
thingsToNotice:
The bedtime titles are the best part: a little demon flying to the moon in a ship of human bones, a baby Beelzebub tucked in under a blanket of damned souls, a grieving fawn who makes a pact and goes on a killing spree. The effect itself is entirely benign, since listeners fall asleep and wake nine hours later feeling rested.

The ending adds a small sting. One story is redacted because it leaks classified details about another anomaly, and another, about a little monster heading home to its mother and countless siblings, is followed shortly by a matching breach elsewhere. The demon answers with writer's small talk about writing what you know, leaving it open whether he predicts, reports or inspires.
